issues.legal_issue: A state-owned corporation may not cancel a retail dealership selection on a technical ground where the applicant timely supplied consents for sufficient family-owned land, the application was accepted and the applicant selected, and the corporation later treated additional co-owner consents as indispensable.
material_facts: The applicant applied for a retail outlet dealership and timely provided consent letters from the family members who owned the land offered for the outlet.
The offered land exceeded the area required, and the corporation inspected the site, accepted the application, interviewed the applicant and selected her.
The corporation later cancelled the selection and reduced the land-and-infrastructure marks to zero because consents from other co-owners had not been submitted by the application deadline.
The corporation relied on additional consent documents submitted after that deadline, although the application and the timely family-member consents had previously been treated as sufficient.
issues.conclusion: The corporation acted arbitrarily and unfairly in cancelling the selection on that technical ground. It was directed to restore the applicant’s appointment.
issues.legal_principle: Under clause 14 of the corporation’s retail outlet selection guidelines, land owned by specified family members may be considered subject to the consent of the concerned family member. Although clause 12 restricts additions or alterations to an application after submission, the corporation could not use the late submission of additional documents to nullify an application that it had initially accepted as meeting the land requirements. A state instrumentality operating in the contractual field must act fairly and treat the applicant fairly, as stated in Mahabir Auto Stores & Ors. v. Indian Oil Corporation and Ors. (1990) 3 SCC 752.

rule.if: retail_dealership_selection_case and state_instrumentality and applicant_selected_after_initial_acceptance and timely_consent_from_relevant_family_landowners and offered_land_sufficient and cancellation_based_on_late_additional_coowner_consents

predicates.retail_dealership_selection_case: The proceeding concerns an applicant’s selection for a retail outlet dealership.
predicates.state_instrumentality: The entity making the selection is an instrumentality of the State.
predicates.applicant_selected_after_initial_accepta: The entity initially accepted the application, assessed the site, and selected the applicant.
predicates.timely_consent_from_relevant_family_land: The applicant submitted by the deadline the consents of the relevant family members who owned the offered land.
predicates.offered_land_sufficient: The offered land met or exceeded the area required for the dealership.
predicates.cancellation_based_on_late_additional_co: The entity cancelled the selection because consents from additional co-owners were not submitted by the deadline, despite the timely consents already provided.

issues.definition: When a state instrumentality initially accepts and selects an applicant who timely provides relevant family-land consents for sufficient land, cancellation based on missing additional co-owner consents submitted late requires the selection to be restored.
